text:
sara: Heads up — Dedicated pool eu-west-2 is seeing a sustained jump in 99th latency starting ~12:12 UTC. Throughput down ~30%. Topline signal: KV cache hit-rate collapsed and eviction rate spiked. Affected tenant looks like t-ignite (very high qps). @jin can you take a look?
ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 latency SLO breach detected (99p > 450ms) — grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/pool-eu-west-2
jin: on it. quick glance at rollout history shows kernel-selector v2.3.1 rolled to pool-eu-west at ~10:45 UTC. hypothesis: selector is picking a slower kernel path (fp16-unfused) for short sequences, causing memcopies and CPU contention. running lightweight profiler now.
miguel: placement data shows t-ignite is heavily consolidated on host-5 alongside two other noisy tenants. affinity for t-ignite is "none" so it got packed. not great. output: `placement show --pool eu-west-2 --host host-5` -> 78% gpu-util, 62% slot-alloc for t-ignite.
kevin: KV metrics attached show `kv_evictions/sec` jumped 20 -> 1200 and `kv_hit_rate` fell 0.78 -> 0.21 around the same time window. excerpt from metrics: ```time,kv_hit_rate,kv_evictions_per_sec
12:00,0.78,18
12:10,0.74,22
12:12,0.31,420
12:20,0.22,980
12:40,0.24,1200
```
jin: profiler snapshot (aggregated stack): ```kernel_selector_choose() 48%
memcpy_device_host 32%
kv_cache_lookup 10%
other 10%``` Looks like kernel selection is dominating and causing more memcopies (host<->device) than before. Also seeing increased context switches on the worker.
eva: we also changed batching wait threshold in prod earlier today to improve tail latency: `batching.max_wait_ms` lowered from 25 -> 10 at 09:30 UTC. That change increases more, smaller batches and may increase GPU kernel churn. could be compounding.
sara: Proposed immediate mitigation steps: 1) pin kernel-selector to v2.2.9 for eu-west dedicated pools 2) temporarily increase KV cache capacity for the pool 3) migrate t-ignite off host-5 to reduce noisy neighbor during remediation. Anyone object?
miguel: no objections. I'll start the placement migration to spread t-ignite: `./scripts/migrate_tenant.sh --tenant t-ignite --target-host host-9 --graceful` (expected 3-4m for draining + warmup).
ops-bot: ACTION: placement migration job queued (job id jm-7782) — miguel started migration at 12:28 UTC.
jin: rolling back kernel-selector to v2.2.9 for pool-eu-west now. command: `platformctl rollout kernel-selector --version v2.2.9 --pool eu-west-2 --force`
ops-bot: DEPLOY: kernel-selector v2.2.9 rolled back on pool-eu-west-2 at 12:45 UTC by miguel (rollback jm-7783).
jin: post-rollback observations: 99p latency returned to baseline within ~2 minutes. metric snapshot: `99p latency 480ms -> 120ms` at 12:47. KV evictions remain elevated though, likely cache cold/warm issues from earlier thrash.
kevin: increased `kv_cache_max_entries` +20% for the pool at 12:50; hit-rate recovered gradually over ~8 minutes. New metrics show `kv_hit_rate` back to ~0.7 by 12:58.
eva: tl;dr: root causes appear to be (1) kernel-selector regression that picks suboptimal kernels for short sequences, (2) a batching config change that increased kernel churn, and (3) placement packing that amplified noisy neighbor effects on host-5 leading to cache thrash.
sara: SLA impact window: 12:12 - 12:50 UTC (~38 minutes). I'm opening an incident report and marking as Sev-2 due to customer-impacting latency on Dedicated. :exclamation:
miguel: follow-ups I'll own: revert automatic batching change in dedicated pools until we have perf tests, add placement guardrails for high-qps tenants, add a migration automation runbook.
jin: perf team follow-ups: add microbenchmark that exercises seq_len < 32 to validate kernel selector choices, add canary gating on kernel-selector rollouts for dedicated pools.
kevin: infra follow-ups: add an alert for `kv_evictions_per_sec > 500` and a dashboard for per-tenant cache metrics; also add an autoscale knob for kv cache size when eviction spike detected.
eva: I'll file a regression ticket against kernel-selector with the profiler output and a failing repro from today. Also add a perf-suite test and schedule a postmortem sync.
sara: thanks all — will update the incident doc with timeline and link postmortem once created. If anyone has logs or small repros (curl commands, configs) drop them here and I'll attach.
